about: The path-shape corpus of the lead policy (T156, standing order 16). The rule is one: every configured and environment path is canonical (canonicalPath in src/sage.js), and the folders that the lead sessions own are real folders of the user, apart from each other and from every denied path. test/t156-path-shapes.test.js applies every shape to every path key: each non-canonical shape must be refused with one line; a canonical path must be accepted, and a probe file written through it must land in the policy's denied (or own) path. The folder rows make each folder that a session uses (the two roots, its own folder and temp folder) in each bad form, refused with one line, and other entries of the roots (another session's folder in any form, a .DS_Store), which the policy does not look at (F-T156-41). The pair rows put two of them in each other; each must be refused with one line. A key that leadPolicy reads must be in keys or in notPaths, so a new path key without its rows fails the test. Reviews block only on a shape missing from this file or a row that fails.

env.PATH: a search list: only its absolute folders are searched, for the claude command, which runs outside the sandbox

host.env: the environment itself; its keys are rows above
host.claude: the claude command, run by the bridge outside the sandbox; no setting of the sandbox comes from it
host.tempRoot: TEMP_ROOT, /private/tmp/sage-lead, fixed in the code; the tests move it; its rows are the folder and pair rows
host.uid: the user's id, from the OS
